value_stream.name: Bulky & White-Goods Delivery, Installation, Haul-Away & Recycling Operations

fields.Owner: Head of Bulky/Home Delivery / Logistics (VS-06) / Commercial
fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), Ecommerce (VS-10), Trade (VS-11), Store Ops (VS-07), Finance (VS-17.4), 3PL (VS-56)
fields.Trigger: Growth in appliance/furniture mix; ecommerce expansion (VS-10); channel strategy review
fields.Volume: Enterprise bulky-delivery program across appliances (1,750 SKUs), furniture (1,750), large-format tile, lumber packs, solar water heaters

workflows.name: Bulky & White-Goods Delivery Program Strategy, Channel Scope & Operating Model

Automation Opportunity: - Bulky-mix/cost scenario modeling; channel profitability by delivery type; auto-flag items requiring specialist install
Controls: - CTL-659 (ensure controlled execution — Bulky/White-Goods Delivery Network, Scheduling & Capacity (PA-143.1).)
- CTL-659: strategy approved (COO); service-scope risk-tiered (W4292); licensed-installer gate (W4293)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06.3 (last-mile), VS-10 (ecommerce), VS-12 (install), VS-32 (returns), VS-56 (3PL), VS-73 (recycle), W4290 (capacity), W4295 (pricing)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-mismatch risk**: in-home install offered where licensing/safety exposure is too high (e.g. split-type AC refrigerant work); mitigated by category-level service-scope gating (W4292) and licensed-installer requirement (W4293)
- **Handoff-ambiguity risk**: install vs deliver vs haul-away ownership unclear → customer ping-pong; mitigated by mapped end-to-end flow & single-bucket order status

steps.activity: Logistics/Commercial set the bulky-delivery strategy — which SKUs/categories are "bulky-deliverable," which channels offer in-home delivery+install, the own-crew vs 3PL mix, and the install/haul-away service scope per category

Logistics/Merchandising map the end-to-end flow (order → schedule → dispatch → deliver → install → haul-away → recycle) and the handoffs to VS-06.3 (last-mile), VS-12 (install), VS-32 (returns), VS-73 (waste/recycle)
Logistics document the strategy, obtain approval, and cascade to capacity (W4290), scheduling (W4291), pricing (W4295), and 3PL terms (W4303)

fields.Participants: DC Ops (VS-04), Store Ops (VS-07), 3PL (VS-56), Finance (VS-17.4), Fleet (VS-06.1)
fields.Volume: Bulky-delivery network across 200 stores / 4 DCs / catchment zones

workflows.name: Bulky Delivery Network, Capacity & Crew Sizing

Automation Opportunity: - Demand-based crew/vehicle sizing; zone heatmap of bulky demand; peak-flex auto-trigger to 3PL
Controls: - CTL-659 (ensure controlled execution — Bulky/White-Goods Delivery Network, Scheduling & Capacity (PA-143.1).)
- CTL-659: capacity sized to forecast with peak flex (3PL); crew shift covers statutory rest (VS-19.3/VS-84)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (logistics), VS-04 (DC), VS-07 (stores), VS-06.1 (fleet), VS-56 (3PL), W4289 (strategy), W4296 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-capacity risk**: peak (summer AC, ber-month furniture) demand exceeds crew capacity → cancellations/lost sales; mitigated by seasonal capacity plan + 3PL flex pool
- **Crew-utilization risk**: oversized own-fleet idles off-peak; mitigated by own-base + 3PL-peak split
System Touchpoints: - Logistics/capacity planning (VS-06); DC/WMS (VS-04); store ops (VS-07); fleet (VS-06.1); 3PL (VS-56); finance (VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Network Planning forecast bulky-delivery volume by zone/category/season (appliance AC peaks in summer, furniture in ber-months) and size crew, vehicle, and lift-gate capacity against the forecast
Network Planning/DC Ops define the staging model — DC-bulked, store-pooled, or cross-dock — and the two-man crew shift pattern covering customer time-windows incl. weekends
steps.r: Network Planning / DC Ops / Store Ops

steps.activity: Network Planning/Finance size own vs 3PL capacity split (build for base, flex to 3PL for peak) and feed capex/lease decisions to VS-06.1/VS-35

fields.Participants: Ecommerce (VS-10), Trade (VS-11), Logistics (VS-06.3), Store Ops (VS-07), Customer

workflows.name: Customer Delivery Scheduling, Time-Window & Routing Management

Automation Opportunity: - Capacity-linked self-service slot booking; auto multi-stop time-window routing; pre-delivery access-check checklist/prompt
Controls: - CTL-659 (ensure controlled execution — Bulky/White-Goods Delivery Network, Scheduling & Capacity (PA-143.1).)
- CTL-659: slots capacity-constrained; pre-delivery access instruction mandatory; confirmation audit-trail
Cross-references: - links to VS-10 (ecommerce), VS-06.3 (routing), VS-13 (service), VS-75 (app), W4290 (capacity), W4297 (dispatch)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-promise risk**: slot sold without real crew capacity → failed window; mitigated by capacity-linked slot calendar (no sell beyond W4290 capacity)
- **Access risk**: customer site unmeasured (door/stair/elevator) → crew cannot deliver; mitigated by mandatory pre-delivery access check & customer instruction
System Touchpoints: - Scheduling/booking engine (VS-10/VS-06); order (VS-16); customer comms (VS-13/VS-75); routing (VS-06.3)

steps.activity: Scheduling system offers the customer available delivery date/time-windows by zone (AM/PM/2-hour slots) constrained by crew/vehicle capacity (W4290) and item install-eligibility (W4292)
Customer confirms slot; system reserves crew+vehicle capacity, sends confirmation + pre-delivery instructions (measure/access/parking), and holds the slot
Logistics auto-routes the day's bulky deliveries into two-man crew manifests (multi-stop, time-window-constrained) and pushes to dispatch (W4297)

fields.Participants: Trade (VS-11), Logistics (VS-06), Compliance (VS-114 for DG), Finance (VS-16)
fields.Trigger: Customer adds bulky/install item to basket (VS-10/VS-11)
fields.Volume: Bulky-order volume (appliances + furniture + large tile + lumber packs)

workflows.name: Bulky Item Order Capture, Eligibility & Pre-Delivery Verification

Automation Opportunity: - Attribute-driven eligibility at basket; installer-availability auto-check; pre-delivery readiness checklist
Controls: - CTL-81 (ensure bulky delivery compliance & e-POD closure.)
- CTL-659: install/DG items installer-gated (W4293); readiness verified; credit cleared (VS-16/VS-68)
Cross-references: - links to VS-01 (item attrs), VS-10/VS-16 (order), VS-114 (DG), VS-68 (credit), W4293 (installers), W4299 (install)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-tagged-item risk**: heavy/gas/refrigerant item sold without install-license gate → unsafe/illegal install; mitigated by SKU attribute gating + installer-availability check
- **Readiness risk**: install attempted at unprepared site → failed/return; mitigated by pre-delivery readiness verification
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising/item master (VS-01/VS-29); ecommerce/order (VS-10/VS-16); logistics (VS-06); compliance DG (VS-114); credit (VS-68)

steps.activity: Merchandising/Delivery Ops tag each bulky SKU with delivery attributes (weight/dim, lift-gate req, two-man flag, install-required flag, install-license req e.g. split-AC refrigerant, haul-away-eligible flag, DG flag)

Order capture enforces eligibility at basket — install/DG items need licensed installer availability (W4293), correct address/zone, stock at serving DC/store, and customer consent for install/haul-away

Delivery Ops verify pre-conditions before confirm — site access, electrical/plumbing readiness for install, payment/credit cleared (VS-16/VS-68), and required permits (e.g. condo delivery elevator booking)

fields.Trigger: Crew onboarding; licensing expiry; new install category
fields.Volume: All bulky-delivery two-man crews + drivers + installers

workflows.name: Two-Man Crew, Driver & Installer Authorization, Training & Certification

Automation Opportunity: - Competency/license registry with expiry auto-alert; auto-block assignment of unlicensed crew to licensed-install orders
Controls: - CTL-81 (ensure bulky delivery compliance & e-POD closure.)
- CTL-659: install work gated by valid license; heavy-lift team-lift + lift-gate; OSH training current (VS-24)
Cross-references: - links to VS-19/VS-98 (crew/contingent), VS-24 (HSE), VS-114 (DG/refrigerant), W4294 (equipment), W4299 (install)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unlicensed-install risk**: split-AC/gas appliance installed by uncertified crew → safety/insurance void + RA 8749 Clean Air Act refrigerant exposure; mitigated by license gate + expiry tracking
- **Injury risk**: manual-handling injury from heavy appliances; mitigated by lift-gate (W4294), team-lift SOP, and OSH training

steps.activity: Delivery Ops/HR authorize each crew member by competency — heavy-lifting/Manual-Handling (DOLE OSH), customer-premises conduct, and specialist install licenses (DTI/TESDA HVAC-refrigerant for split-AC, gas/electrical for cookers/water heaters)
HSE/HR train crews on heavy-lifting technique, appliance securing, DG items, and customer-premises safety/liability (coordinate VS-24/VS-98 for outsourced crews)
Delivery Ops/Compliance track license/cert expiry, enforce no-work-without-valid-cert, and revoke authorization on breach

fields.Trigger: Capacity plan (W4290); fleet lifecycle; equipment failure
fields.Volume: Bulky-delivery vehicle fleet + lift-gates + handling equipment

workflows.name: Delivery Vehicle, Equipment & Lift-Gate Fleet Provisioning

Automation Opportunity: - Item-dimension → vehicle-type auto-assignment; PM-triggered availability; pre-trip inspection checklist app
Controls: - CTL-659 (ensure controlled execution — Bulky/White-Goods Delivery Network, Scheduling & Capacity (PA-143.1).)
- CTL-659: vehicle type matches item dims; lift-gate/strap PM current; pre-trip inspection logged
Cross-references: - links to VS-06.1 (fleet), VS-35 (asset), VS-40 (capex), VS-20.3/VS-138 (maintenance), VS-24 (HSE), W4290 (capacity)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wrong-vehicle risk**: parcel van dispatched for a refrigerator → damage/inability; mitigated by item-dimension-driven vehicle assignment
- **Equipment-failure risk**: lift-gate/strap failure drops an appliance → injury + damage; mitigated by PM schedule + pre-trip inspection
Time Estimate: - Provisioning per lifecycle; PM/inspection ~15–30 min/vehicle pre-trip

steps.activity: Fleet/Delivery Ops specify and provision the right vehicle mix (lift-gate trucks for appliances, box trucks for furniture, flatbeds for lumber/large tile) with securing equipment (straps, blankets, dollies, appliance hand-trucks)

steps.a: Head of Bulky Delivery / Asset Mgr
steps.activity: Fleet/Asset register vehicles/equipment in the asset system, schedule preventive maintenance (lift-gate hydraulics, straps), and inspect before deployment
HSE/Fleet equip crews with required PPE and handling aids (back-support, gloves, steel-toe), and replace worn/damaged equipment before failure

workflows.name: Bulky Delivery Pricing, Fee & Zone Structure

Automation Opportunity: - Zone-cost-to-serve modeling; fee-vs-conversion A/B; RA leakage detection on delivery/install/haul-away fees
Controls: - CTL-659 (ensure controlled execution — Bulky/White-Goods Delivery Network, Scheduling & Capacity (PA-143.1).)
- CTL-659: fees cost-recovery-justified; RA-monitored (VS-118); incentives conversion-tested
Cross-references: - links to VS-01.2 (pricing), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-10 (ecommerce), VS-14/VS-58 (marketing), W4289 (strategy), W4310 (recycle economics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-recovery risk**: delivery fee below cost-to-serve → margin leak; mitigated by zone-cost fee & RA monitoring (VS-118)
- **Cart-abandonment risk**: high fee suppresses bulky conversion; mitigated by threshold/bundle incentive design
System Touchpoints: - Pricing/merchandising (VS-01.2); revenue assurance (VS-118); ecommerce (VS-10); finance (VS-17.4); marketing (VS-14)

steps.activity: Pricing/Finance determine bulky cost-to-serve by zone/category (vehicle, crew, install, haul-away, recycle, failed-window cost) and set zone-tiered delivery fees and free-delivery thresholds, aligned to VS-118
Pricing/Merchandising set install-fee, haul-away-fee, and bundle incentives (free install with appliance bundle) to drive attach without margin leak, aligned to VS-14/VS-58
Revenue Assurance/Pricing monitor fee recovery vs cost-to-serve, detect leakage (override, under-charge), and tune thresholds

fields.Participants: DC Ops (VS-04), Store Ops (VS-07), 3PL (VS-56), CX (VS-13), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Trigger: Operating performance; peak season planning; SLA review

workflows.name: Bulky Delivery Service-Level, Capacity Analytics & Peak (Ber-Month) Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Real-time SLA dashboard; auto-peak-flex trigger; capacity-vs-demand alerting; NPS-by-delivery-type analytics
Controls: - CTL-659 (ensure controlled execution — Bulky/White-Goods Delivery Network, Scheduling & Capacity (PA-143.1).)
- CTL-659: SLA monitored monthly; peak plan approved; failed/damaged deliveries reviewed & recovered
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (logistics), VS-13 (CX), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-24 (HSE), VS-56 (3PL), W4290 (capacity), W4300 (damage), W4312 (program analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **SLA-drift risk**: failed-window/damage rate rising unflagged → CX/repeat-purchase loss; mitigated by monthly SLA dashboard + corrective action
- **Peak-capacity risk**: ber-month/summer demand exceeds capacity → cancellations; mitigated by annual peak plan + 3PL pre-booking
System Touchpoints: - Logistics analytics (VS-06); CX/NPS (VS-13); finance (VS-17.4); 3PL (VS-56); HSE incidents (VS-24)
Time Estimate: - Monthly review ~1–2 days; annual peak plan ~2–3 weeks

steps.activity: Delivery Ops/Analytics track SLA KPIs (on-time-window %, first-time-success %, install-complete %, failed-window %, damage-on-delivery %, haul-away completion %) and crew/vehicle utilization vs plan
Delivery Ops/Commercial run the annual peak plan (summer AC, ber-month furniture/appliance) — pre-book 3PL flex, pre-position stock at serving DCs, extend crew shifts within DOLE limits
Finance/CX review cost-per-delivery, NPS for delivered orders, and recovery/refund from failed/damaged deliveries, and feed improvement actions to W4297–W4312
